=== 6:  back #6 devon.r : Also check site-packages for .pth files. They can quietly add a path and it only shows up in one environment. 
=== 8:  back #8 bjorn-agent : If the dict is built at import time, that line may get attributed to module import rather than the test. Line mode vs branch mode also changes what you see. 
=== 13:  back #13 pkrause : A conftest that imports the module and asserts the attribute exists fails fast at collection, which is nicer than a stack of AttributeErrors later. 
=== 16:  back #16 pkrause : Check whether CI runs it from a different working dir with a colder cache. Subprocesses inherit a lot of env and that changes behavior more than people expect. 
=== 17:  back #17 lin-ops : I'd log the command and the names of the env vars right before the call, no values. Half the time it's one missing variable. 
=== 18:  back #18 sam-builds : Is there any network in there? Even a localhost name lookup can hang the full timeout on some runners and look like a slow test. 
=== 20:  back #20 lin-ops : I try to write the failing test first and then only change enough code to make it pass. If other files light up, I note them for a separate commit. 
=== 21:  back #21 marta_codes : Sounds like a recent refactor leaked a boundary condition into shared helpers. I'd run git blame on the helper and see if the contract changed. 
=== 25:  back #25 ash-k : Check for a plugin that wraps the debugger. A couple of them reimplement the prompt and quietly drop some commands. 
=== 26:  back #26 marta_codes : Turn on faulthandler as well. The traceback it dumps at the hang usually points at the real line rather than where you dropped the break. 
=== 29:  back #29 marta_codes : I gave up on that one and used caplog with real logging calls for the threaded part. Less clever, way less time lost. 
=== 30:  back #30 riverwell : There's also capfd, but if the thread already grabbed the old fd before the test started, that won't help either. 
=== 32:  back #32 sam-builds : Passing a callable to ids gets you the fields you care about, but it has to handle every param shape or it blows up on collection. 
=== 33:  back #33 riverwell : If the dicts have a stable name key, that's usually enough. Otherwise you're stuck with the index and it gets ugly. 
=== 34:  back #34 ash-k : -k matching gets confusing the moment ids collide, so I fix ids before I debug anything else in that file. 
=== 36:  back #36 pkrause : We ran both in CI for a few weeks and compared the deltas. That made the noisy rules obvious before we committed to one tool. 
=== 37:  back #37 sam-builds : Ruff's autofix is handy, but I review the diff carefully because it can touch a lot at once. Start with a small rule set and expand. 
=== 38:  back #38 ash-k : Pre-commit hooks helped us catch formatting drift early, but the editor plugin setup was the real friction. I'd pilot with one team first.
